Zverev now leads Shelton 6-0, a comfortable match-up for the German who served far better than Shelton, remained far steadier from the baseline and, as usual, nullified the effects of the left-hander’s forehand with the quality of his elite two-handed backhand.In a match between two of the biggest servers, the first job for both players was to take care of his service. A visibly tense Shelton served terribly during the decisive moments of the first set, double-faulting on break point in the first game of the match. Shelton then double-faulted on set point to hand over a second break. He was no match for Zverev from the baseline, and his forehand was far too erratic. Zverev, meanwhile, served extremely well throughout the match, landing 69% of first serves and winning 85% of first-serve points.Shelton managed to build rhythm behind his service games in set two, putting Zverev under some pressure by forcing a tie-break, but the German handled the most important moment of the match well. He snatched the first mini-break with an excellent forehand passing-shot winner off a timid approach from Shelton, then he ended a similarly tense exchange with a vicious down-the-line forehand to take the second mini-break. Two big unreturned serves later, Zverev led 5-0 in the tie-break and the set was all but over.Although Shelton worked hard to force a fourth set, it did not take long for Zverev to close out a victory that appeared inevitable from the first game.View image in fullscreenBen Shelton was left face down after one gruelling rally.Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPAThis match was a fitting ending to a dreary grand slam season on the ATP tour that has been dictated by the injuries and physical issues suffered by Carlos Alcaraz, who returned from a long injury layoff at this tournament, and Jannik Sinner. Their challenges presented so many players at the top of the sport with golden opportunities to step up and compete for major titles, but so few of them over the past five months even managed to put themselves in real contention. Zverev has been rewarded for his consistency and ability to continue to put himself in positive positions deep in the majors. Each victory has clearly strengthened him mentally.For plenty of tennis fans and viewers around the world, however, no amount of on-court success can erase the discomfort that comes with seeing Zverev succeed. He has been accused by two of his former girlfriends, Olya Sharypova and Brenda Patea, of physical abuse. In June 2024, during his run to the French Open final, Zverev settled an assault case against him in Germanyfor allegedly pushing and strangling Patea, his ex-girlfriend and the mother of their daughter. The case was declared no verdict, with a court spokesperson stating: “The truth remains open.” Zverev denied those charges and he has denied all allegations against him.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFastPasses, Mega Honey Deuces and $55 chopped cheese: welcome to the US Open in 2041 | Bryan Armen GrahamRead moreAt the Australian Open last year, Zverev was heckled by a fan before his trophy ceremony speech, with the fan declaring: “Australia believes Olya and Brenda.” Zverev’s three grand slam finals this year have progressed without issue and he remains a popular player at major tournaments.For Shelton, who began his North American hard court swing attempting to recover from a painful first round loss at Wimbledon, the greatest summer of his career included a second Masters 1000 title at the Canadian Open, a first grand slam final and a new career high ranking of No 4.His success is testament to his continued improvement and at 23 years old there is much more to come. However, some of those deficiencies, particularly his ground game and return of serve, can still be exposed by the elite, as it was during his lonely Sunday afternoon inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026US Open tennisTennisUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: USA defend Fiba Women’s World Cup title after early scare against France | Fiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 | The Guardian
description: The USA overcame a 14-point France lead in the first half, with Breanna Stewart scoring 22 en route to the comeback win
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The USA overcame a 14-point France lead in the first half, with Breanna Stewart scoring 22 en route to the comeback win
Content: The USA haven’t lost a game at the Olympics or World Cup in 20 years.Photograph: Maryam Majd/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe USA haven’t lost a game at the Olympics or World Cup in 20 years.Photograph: Maryam Majd/ReutersFiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026USA defend Fiba Women’s World Cup title after early scare against FranceUSA overcame a 14-point France lead in first halfBreanna Stewart scores 22 points; Caitlin Clark gets 12AgenciesSun 13 Sep 2026 16.35 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 16.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDefending champions USA fell behind early but stormed back past ⁠France 97-79 on Sunday to win the Women’s World Cup.In a rematch of the 2024 ⁠Olympic final, ⁠the ​American women came out on top once more, earning their fifth consecutive World Cup title ⁠and stretching their impressive unbeaten run at Olympics or World Cups to 20 years.Cathy Engelbert’s WNBA tenure: the wins and losses that defined her seven yearsRead moreThe perennial red-hot favourites, who had not lost a World Cup match since 2006, the USA were below their best for much of the tournament. They came into Sunday’s game looking vulnerable, having come close to defeats against unheralded Italy andagain against Spain in the semi-finals.No team had come within 20 points of France as they cruised into a maiden World Cup final, and they started strong on Sunday.The US trailed by two points at half-time to an energetic France side but turned it on when it mattered, outscoring the Europeans 30-12 in the third quarter.The French had ⁠to settle for silver in their best ‌ever World Cup finish, despite ‌leading by 14 points at one stage.View image in fullscreenGabby Williams led France in a first-half flurry that put the US in comeback mode.Photograph: Ebrahim Noroozi/APUSA captain Breanna Stewart, ‌top scorer with 22 points, helped her team carve out an early five-point lead, anchoring the scoring in the beginning stages.But the French exploded into action, quickly found their three-point range and, led by Gabby Williams, went on a ‌21-2 rampage that saw them open up that 14-point advantage early in the second quarter.The Americans ​started chipping away at the lead and trailed by just two points at the break afterCaitlin Clarkhit a massively important three-pointer at the buzzer.France were seeking revenge for their one-point loss in the gold medal match at the Paris Olympics but lost their composure as the Americans turned on the afterburners in the second half.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionConsecutive triples from Kahleah Copper and ⁠Jackie Young gave Team USA a 58-51 lead ​and they never ​looked back, with another ​Clark three-pointer stretching their lead to 19 points ​at the ‌start of the ​fourth quarter. ​The French could not break past a hard-working defence.Earlier on Sunday, Spain soothed the disappointment of their narrow semi-final loss to the US by claiming bronze with an 81-58 win over Germany.The Spanish went close to a major boilover on Saturday, pushing the heavily favoured Americans all the way in their semi-final, levelling the scores at 58-58 three-quarters of the way through the match, before the US pulled away.On Sunday, Spain were in control throughout against the spirited but limited hosts, who had never reached the final four of the tournament as a unified country.Top-scorer Iyana Martin was one assist away from a double-double, with 20 points while grabbing a game-best nine dimes.Explore more on these topicsFiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026BasketballCaitlin ClarkUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winner | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Pro Ref has admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have counted after the VAR ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Pro Ref has admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have counted after the VAR ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup
Content: Enzo Fernández dives at the ball from an offside position as Lisandro Martínez appeals, before Erling Haaland turns in Manchester City’s winner.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEnzo Fernández dives at the ball from an offside position as Lisandro Martínez appeals, before Erling Haaland turns in Manchester City’s winner.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesManchester United‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winnerOfficiating body announces it will review the incidentUnhappy Carrick says error was ‘as obvious as it gets’Jamie Jacksonat Old TraffordSun 13 Sep 2026 17.31 EDTFirst published on Sun 13 Sep 2026 15.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePro Ref admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have been allowed after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the build-up. The elite officiating body will review the decision and has contactedManchester United.Manchester City recover from Foden red card as Haaland wins derby at UnitedRead moreHaaland’s 60th minute goal forManchester Cityat Old Trafford was initially ruled offside before the VAR’s intervention. It came after Josko Gvardiol’s cross hit Patrick Dorgu’s boot, passed Fernández and the United defender Lisandro Martínez, and was finished by the City No 9. VAR decided Fernández was not interfering despite Martínez marking the midfielder.A Pro Ref statement said: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.“The on-field decision was offside against Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.“In the same attack, it was established that Fernández did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”After the match but before the Pro Ref statement, an unhappyMichael Carrickexpressed concern over Haaland’s winner.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“At the time I hadn’t totally seen it. But the explanation I got was he wasn’t interfering with play, so I just don’t get it,” the United manager said. “I can’t understand how they’re trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, screens, and so many whatever offices to try and come up with the right decisions.“If that’s how the rules are interpreted, that you’re not interfering with play because you’ve thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Lisandro has to react from – it’s worrying if that’s really how the game’s seen by those who are officiating it.”Carrick was asked if an apology from Pro Ref would be welcome. “Yeah, that’d be great, that. Yeah, I can’t wait for that one,” he said. “I don’t really know how you go and get another explanation on that one. I think we all understand what that rule means [regarding interfering with play], and it’s pretty obvious. It’s as obvious as it gets.”Enzo Maresca, though, was adamant that Fernández was not interfering. “Yeah – and the fourth official said Erling is onside,” the City manager said.The 199th Manchester derby’s other controversial decision was Phil Foden’s 23rd-minute red card. The forward kicked Bruno Fernandes in the stomach, but only after United’s captain had kicked him. Maresca backed Michael Oliver’s red card but suggested the referee should also have sent off Fernandes.“Phil Foden red card is a red card, but I also think it is red card from Bruno,” City’s manager said. “Reviewing the action, it is a clear red card for Phil because it is a reaction but you can also see Bruno’s [action].”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick looks on from the touchline during the Manchester derby.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianCity now have 12 points, second only to Arsenal on goal difference, while United have only four points and are 13th. “We will get there, I’m convinced of that,” Carrick said.“We haven’t got as many points as we wanted and we should have. We’ve got to accept that and take that. It doesn’t change us moving forward and our hopes for the season and what we can achieve as a team. We’ve made really good strides over a period of time and we will continue to do that.”Carrick was asked about the pre-game protest against the club’s move to eradicate ticket touts that some believe to be draconian. United said on Friday that 685 accounts had been subject to a ban and 464 supporters had received a reduced sanction or final warning.Carrick said: “The details in terms of all what goes behind it, I’m not always in line to get to the bottom of it, but I definitely appreciate the supporters.“If they do feel [unhappy] in certain ways then, of course, we want to try everything to make them happy. That’s part of performances on the pitch and off the pitch. That’s obvious. They’re a huge part of this football club. They’re everything for this football club.”Inside the stadium The Red Army hung a banner over the tunnel that said, “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace.” All usual banners were removed from the Stretford End.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickEnzo MarescaManchester CityErling HaalandRefereesVideo assistant referees (VARs)newsShareReuse this content

title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chants | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Al-Nassr’s Cristiano Ronaldo has called on the Saudi Pro League to act after Rúben Neves was subjected to chants about Diogo Jota during a match
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Al-Nassr’s Cristiano Ronaldo has called on the Saudi Pro League to act after Rúben Neves was subjected to chants about Diogo Jota during a match
Content: Al-Nassr’s Cristiano Ronaldo played alongside Diogo Jota with the Portugal national team.Photograph: Hamad I Mohammed/ReutersView image in fullscreenAl-Nassr’s Cristiano Ronaldo played alongside Diogo Jota with the Portugal national team.Photograph: Hamad I Mohammed/ReutersSoccerCristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chantsAl-Hilal’s Rúben Neves subjected to chants at Al-TaawounNeves was close friend of Jota and pallbearer at funeralReutersSun 13 Sep 2026 10.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCristiano Ronaldo said that fans who appeared to ⁠make chants referencing his former teammate Diogo Jota at Rúben Neves during a Saudi ⁠Pro League ⁠match ​should be banned for life from football stadiums.The chants occurred on Saturday during ⁠a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves’s side,Al-Hilal, in Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.‘Forever 20’: Liverpool release images of memorial to Diogo Jota and André SilvaRead moreJota died last yearin a car crash in Zamora, ​north-western Spain, along with ‌his brother André ‌Silva. A close friend of Jota, Neves was a ‌pallbearer at his funeral.Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting “Jota”. The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and ‌then up to the sky in response. Passing through the mixed zone after the game, ​Neves said: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account. “The league must take ⁠action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” he wrote. “This ​is no longer football, ​and there have to be limits. People ​who behave ‌like this should ​never ​be allowed to enter a stadium again.“The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.Reuters has contacted Al-Taawoun and Al-Hilal for comment.Explore more on these topicsFootballCristiano RonaldoDiogo JotaAl-HilalSaudi Pro LeagueSaudi Arabia and sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Enric Mas reigns supreme at last in Vuelta a España to delight Spanish fans | Vuelta a España | The Guardian
description: The Spanish rider Enric Mas secured his first Vuelta a España title on Sunday as Tobias Johannessen won the 21st and final stage in Granada
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Spanish rider Enric Mas secured his first Vuelta a España title on Sunday as Tobias Johannessen won the 21st and final stage in Granada
Content: Enric Mas (centre) flanked by second-placed Primoz Roglic (left) and third-placed Felix Gall. ‘I’ve dreamed of this and fought for it,’ said the Spaniard.Photograph: Gregorio Marrero/APView image in fullscreenEnric Mas (centre) flanked by second-placed Primoz Roglic (left) and third-placed Felix Gall. ‘I’ve dreamed of this and fought for it,’ said the Spaniard.Photograph: Gregorio Marrero/APVuelta a EspañaEnric Mas reigns supreme at last in Vuelta a España to delight Spanish fansMas wins title after three second-place finishesTobias Johannessen takes final stage in GranadaAgence France-PresseSun 13 Sep 2026 15.30 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSpain’s Enric Mas secured his firstVuelta a Españatitle on Sunday as Tobias Johannessen won the 21st and final stage in Granada, bringing the three-week Grand Tour to a close.The 31-year-old, who took the red jersey after Tadej Pogacar abandoned the race after a crash on stage eight, held off the four-time champion Primoz Roglic to become the first Spaniard to win the Vuelta since Alberto Contador in 2014.Mas, a three-time Vuelta runner-up, finished 2min 15sec ahead of Roglic in the general classification, with Felix Gall third, a further half-minute behind.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Mas crossed the finish line arm-in-arm with his six Movistar teammates stretched out beside him. It was the Spaniard’s first Grand Tour triumph, which he effectively sealed by limiting his losses to Roglic in the individual time trialon Thursdayand then expanding his lead on Saturday in thelast mountain stage.“I’ve dreamed of this and fought for it,” said Mas. “I felt some nerves, it was a day with a mix of emotions, all of them positive.“We have to keep on doing what we’re doing, we’re sportsmen and it’s like this – we’re thinking about the next objectives and we have no time to enjoy our victories.”View image in fullscreenMas crosses the finish line in Granada arm-in-arm with his six Movistar teammates.Photograph: Marcelo del Pozo/ReutersThe Norwegian Johannessen prevailed in the 112km final stage, which started in a supermarket and featured a series of loops through Granada and around the Alhambra palace. The Uno-X Mobility rider held off Alessandro Romele and Ramses Debruyne in a sprint finish.The last 9.8km of the race was neutralised earlier on Sunday in agreement with the governing body, the UCI, after riders raised safety concerns, so for the general classification contenders it was a procession to the finish line.Mas inherited the red jersey from Pogacar after the Slovene, who was the overwhelming favourite to triumph at the Vuelta for the first time, suffered a severe crash which ended his season. Five-time Tour de France winner Pogacar was hoping to become only the fourth rider to claim a Tour-Vuelta double in the same season.A runner-up in 2018, 2021 and 2022, Mas fended off attacks from Roglic and Gall along the way and proved a worthy winner, rising to every challenge. It was Team Movistar’s first Vuelta win since Colombia’s Nairo Quintana claimed victory in 2016.“The reality is that the team needed a victory like this, and now we have it,” said Mas.Explore more on these topicsVuelta a EspañaCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arteta embraces perfect storm to play the victim in game of his own making | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Refereeing is now an impossible job owing to the culture of micro-analysis the Arsenal manager has helped to create
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Refereeing is now an impossible job owing to the culture of micro-analysis the Arsenal manager has helped to create
Content: Mikel Arteta took issue with Sunderland’s penalty award in Arsenal’s win on Saturday.Photograph: Ian Hodgson/APView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta took issue with Sunderland’s penalty award in Arsenal’s win on Saturday.Photograph: Ian Hodgson/APPremier LeagueAnalysisArteta embraces perfect storm to play the victim in game of his own makingBarney RonayRefereeing is now an impossible job owing to the culture of micro-analysis the Arsenal manager has helped to createSun 13 Sep 2026 16.35 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTShareA gentleman is never rude unintentionally, only by design. Nobody really knows who said this first. But it could easily be a line from the Elite Football Manager’s Guide to Press Conferences (Premier League edition). Because nothing happens by accident in these spaces.Every word spoken in front of the board covered in adverts is metered and planned. A manager is never angry, or concerned, or even charming unintentionally. The gameisthe game, but so are all the other bits spilling out either side of it.‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winnerRead moreIt was hard not to think about this while listening to Mikel Arteta talk about thepenalty awarded to Sunderlandat the Stadium of Light for a perceived act of grappling on Dan Ballard by Ezri Konsa. This is said with genuine professional respect. As everyone who has ever done a podcast knows – and this is, let’s be clear, everyone – there are lost Amazonian tribes discussing Girls season three in their own dark corner of Spotify – there are moments when you just have to flip the switch, up the energy and turn on full clip‑this‑bit‑up‑please‑Dave sincerity mode.Arteta did this beautifully in the moment, appearing genuinely struck by what he was saying, radiating wounded integrity, like a disappointed junior headmaster appealing for the return of the school minibus keys.Let’s be clear though. Arteta is not “very worried” about all this. He’s not “sad” or indeed, as he later emphasised for good measure, “really sad”. He’s not concerned solely with “protecting the game”, speaking here for all of us, just a fan of football.Come off it. This is a manager we know to be obsessed with the most marginal of gains, to micro-plan the micro-details. As is all elite sport now. There has been talk of rowing coaches installing fibreglass toilet seats at their training hubs having calculated the average athlete spends 20 minutes in there and this is all key glute management time. Arteta loves this stuff. There’s no way Ben White isn’t sat fiddling with his phone at the training ground on a gold-standard Easy‑Cup Mega-Soft Evacu-Throne.So it is with his public statements. This will have all been gamed and contingency‑planned in advance. And for hard, rational, tactical reasons, because this is how the game is played and run now. So what does it mean?View image in fullscreenEzri Konsa is penalised for a contentious foul on Dan Ballard in the box.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/ShutterstockThere are three things we know for sure. First, Arteta was right. This was a bad refereeing decision. Most obviously it was factually wrong. Ballard very skilfully pulled Konsa down on top of him, while simultaneously feigning shock that such a thing could happen.It was doubly bad because the referee’s response was pre-planned, flagged by the early-season chat about refereeing in a more interventionist fashion. Go into any situation with a voice in your head, a vaguely worded mission to fulfil: this will skew your judgment.The second thing is that referees are not biased. They’re just not very good. Two things have happened to them. First, the barrage of information to be absorbed in real time during a game is now utterly mind-boggling.Most referees are not from a high-pressure data-processing background. These are not military pilots or traders on a currency floor. Less than a quarter have an academic degree. The task is beyond them. This is not a slur or an insult. It’s a simple description of what is happening, as supported by the evidence.This is doubly annoying because referees have become fundamentally confused about their role.Refereesare not ringmasters, or curators of the spectacle. They don’t get to decide what our sport should look like. Pro Ref is a private company with nolocus standito rule on the aesthetics of football. A referee should exist at the very edge of the spectacle. You’re not a local government planning officer with a mandate to decide which double-glazed French doors are or aren’t in character with the neighbourhood. Stop getting football not just wrong, butwrong.View image in fullscreenMikel Arteta has a word with the fourth official, Elliot Bell, at Sunderland.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersBut Arteta was also ready for this. Arsenal’s coaches will have known this would happen at some point. That press conference response was already in the chamber. Arteta may even have practised his sad-not-angry face, his key lines.And this would be the correct thing to do. None of this is breaking the rules, just as Arsenal are not a dirty team or a bunch of cheats. They play the game that is being presented to us, a sport that is being made to operate at the edge of its own ludicrously micro‑analysed rules on small issues of physical contact.Arteta’s Arsenal have been masterful at finding advantages in this. Defenders are very good at playing with the ball at their feet now. Defenders are not selected for their ability to resist physical challenges. It is logical to exploit this, just as it is logical to seek to protect your ability to do so by speaking in public about how the rules are applied. This is why Arteta is good, and why he wins.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIt is also true that this has created a strange environment. The tone of the wider Arsenal fanbase is another element here. There is no one type of football fan. All human life is here. But the fact remains, the loudest voices in the online Arsenal hive mind, even the atmosphere in the stadium is unique in its absolute conviction of victimhood, of conspiracy, of a galvanising sense of adversity.There is no other ground where every single refereeing decision, even the who-knows 50-50s, is so violently and eloquently disputed. There are supporters who seem to spend most of the game up on their feet in a state of performative, weaponised indignation, whose entire interaction with the spectacle is an attitude of aggrieved injustice.This makes sense, too. It speaks directly to the game we have created. Aggrieved middle-aged rule pedantry. This is the new cauldron of hate.View image in fullscreenSet-piece grappling was a theme once more in Arsenal’s win at Sunderland.Photograph: Ian Hodgson/APIs it based in reality? Not perhaps on the outline numbers. Arsenal have been awarded more fouls than any other team this season. Only six teams last season had more fouls awarded against them, and the same the year before. They had the fewest yellow cards last season. They haven’t had a single red since they had six of them in 2024‑25.Still, certain key incidents continue to grate and fester. There was the incorrectly denied penalty claim for Bruno Guimarãesat Aston Villa. The balls-up with VAR lines against Brentford in 2023, which, if it really was deliberate conspiracy-cheating, was the worst, most public attempt at deliberate conspiracy-cheating ever conceived.There is discontent at the way some rules seem to be applied more severely to Arsenal, the silly little stuff like delaying or fiddling about with restarts. But then again, if you make the game about that, if you plan to play on the margins, and successfully so, more stuff might happen in that place while you’re doing it.Arteta has also played the role of arms-length rage conjurer expertly, has gone from rarely commenting on referees to heartfelt and carefully targeted critic. TheSunderlandpenalty award was a first opportunity to unload on the refereeing backlash to Arsenal’s tactics, to launch his pre-prepared defence; and to point out something demonstrably true. Referees have lost control of this, because the game has got beyond them.In many ways this was a perfect storm for Arteta. Not just a decision that didn’t matter, because the penalty was saved. But a decision that was clearly incorrect too, a chance to get your lobbying in while very obviously in the right.There will be more of this as the season plays out, as Arsenal work to preserve the advantages they have made for themselves in close quarters, tactical attack and defence. Factor in that masterful turn at a press conferencej’accuse, and Saturday was a significant win in more ways than one.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueMikel ArtetaArsenalSunderlandRefereesanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Kimi Antonelli holds off Max Verstappen during Madring debut to win F1 Spanish GP | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: Predictions that Formula One’s newest circuit in Madrid would make for a prosaic affair proved correct with only four on-track passes
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Predictions that Formula One’s newest circuit in Madrid would make for a prosaic affair proved correct with only four on-track passes
Content: Kimi Antonelli has become the first driver to win the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit in Madrid.Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/ReutersView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli has become the first driver to win the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit in Madrid.Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/ReutersFormula One 2026Kimi Antonelli holds off Max Verstappen during Madring debut to win F1 Spanish GPMcLaren’s Norris in third and Ferrari’s Leclerc fourthTrack design questioned owing to lack of overtakingGiles Richardsat the MadringSun 13 Sep 2026 11.38 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKimi Antonelli’s seemingly inexorable march to his first Formula One world championship advanced at double time as the young Italian proved to have good fortune on his side too with his victory at the Spanish Grand Prix.His execution was perfect as he became the first driver to win at F1’s newest circuit, the Madring, in beating Red Bull’sMax Verstappeninto second and McLaren’s Lando Norris into third. But Antonelli’s win came at a cost to Norris who, while having led until lap 14 and was impressively quick, was just unlucky and try as he might was left tilting at windmills in Madrid.‘No stopping him’: Hamilton admits defeat as Antonelli charges towards F1 world titleRead moreThat Norris could not at least fight back came after the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car (VSC). It cost him because he passed the pit lane entry a fraction after it was called. This was a factor in what was something of an indictment of abrand new circuit– built at enormous expense but whose design has contrived to make overtaking all but impossible.It was at best a prosaic procession and at times a snooze in the sunshine as there were just a handful, not even double figures, of on‑track passes after the opening lap and none of them at the sharp end. A remarkable occurrence this season given the extent that the new engine formula has promoted repeated changes of position, so much so that it has become known as yo-yo racing. That wasn’t the case in Madrid.The field largely circulated managing their rubber, with controlled gaps between them, barely able to close and with almost no passes.Even before the weekend began drivers had questioned whether overtaking would be possible just from their experience on simulators. As they took to the track their instincts proved all too prescient. The high-speed layout is compromised by braking zones angled in to many of the corners. It requires drivers to brake while turning in, removing the option of putting a car alongside by outbraking an opponent. While allowing for only one line into the corner this is easily defended by the leading car.Verstappen, who had been outspoken in his criticism of the design and predicted a procession, said the track designers had made mistakes.View image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli’s win further extends his lead at the top of the F1 standings.Photograph: Jon Nazca/Reuters“You can’t overtake,” he said. “In terms of track design, I think it can be better. Input from drivers in the future on track design can also help a lot. I know they will always come back to you and say: ‘Yeah, but the space’. But that’s BS. There’s always a way to find an overtaking opportunity around a track.”It also played a factor in that had there been even a sniff of a chance of passing, Norris might at very least have enjoyed a fightback, certainly he had the pace.Instead he was left frustrated. “Not a lot we could do … load of shit,” he said. “Just take it on the chin. We were too quick, that’s all it was. Very unlucky today, guys – we deserved the win quite easily.”Norris, the defending world champion, looked to have the race in hand while leading until it turned on lap 14 when the VSC was called to deal with Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin which had gone into the barriers. It was called just seconds after Norris had passed the pit entrance, prompting his point that it would have been advantageous to be slightly slower.Antonelli behind him dived in for a cheap stop and new tyres as did Verstappen, andMcLarencommitted to pitting Norris at the end of the lap but the timing was disastrous. The VSC ended just before he came in and then, to add insult to injury, his stop was slow at a full seven seconds.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWhen Norris crawled out, his lead was gone with Antonelli and Verstappen gaining track position in front of him.While Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc had stayed out and led the field, they proceeded to circulate with somnolent metronomy, waiting for the Monégasque to stop. He did and the three frontrunners continued line astern to the flag. It was impossible not to consider that on another track Norris would have had a shot at trying to pass but it was a forlorn hope in Madrid.Even Antonelli conceded Norris had been dealt a poor hand. “It doesn’t feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win,” he said. “But overall we’ll take it.”Indeed he will, as a spot of luck tends to ride with world champions, which he is on course to be, given his title lead. Especially after his teammate George Russell, on a two-stop strategy that did not pay off, could manage only fifth. Another hammer blow to the British driver who, with seven career victories, has one fewer than the eight Antonelli now has this season.Antonelli’s lead over the second‑placed Russell is now 81 points. Lewis Hamilton, who had to retire on lap six with a brake problem is third, 101 behind, while Norris is 106 behind in fourth, with nine meetings remaining.A disappointing opening for a new circuit then but a familiar finish as Antonelli once more closed out in control. A driver who will not care at all that it was his least entertaining win of the season.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Kimi AntonelliMax VerstappenLando NorrisMercedes GPMcLarenRed BullnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lewis Dunk’s showstopper helps five-star Brighton to rout 10-man Coventry | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Coventry’s winless and goalless start to the Premier League season continued with a 5-0 home thrashing at the hands of Brighton
Author: Ben Bloom
Headline: Coventry’s winless and goalless start to the Premier League season continued with a 5-0 home thrashing at the hands of Brighton
Content: Brighton’s players gather around Lewis Dunk after his stunning fourth goal.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenBrighton’s players gather around Lewis Dunk after his stunning fourth goal.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAPremier LeagueLewis Dunk’s showstopper helps five-star Brighton to rout 10-man CoventryBen Bloomat the Coventry Building Society ArenaSun 13 Sep 2026 11.10 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe bare facts are bleak: Coventry City are only the second team inPremier Leaguehistory to lose their first four games of the season ­without scoring a goal. “And yet …” will be the enduring message from Frank ­Lampard to his players.And yet they have caused prob­lems for opposition teams. And yet they have already faced three of the top flight’s European contingent. And yet they are not altogether playing that badly – the Brighton goalkeeper Bart ­Verbruggen being named player of the match can attest to that. But Coventry des­perately need a point, or even a goal, to give their ­confidence a much-needed boost. It does not take long for a promoted club’s relegation fears to turn to reality.Rangers lay down Old Firm marker as Celtic sent packing from Scottish League CupRead moreGoals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouyé, Lewis Dunk – especially – and Yasin Ayari were all moments of individual brilliance. But there was also a sense of Coventry self-destruction, with no complaints from Lampard over Taiwo Awoniyi’s red card for an elbow into Maxim De Cuyper’s face, nor the penalty conceded by Bobby Thomas for Pascal Gross to score the ­visitors’ third. There are also legitimate questions to be asked of Lampard’s decision to maintain an attacking approach even after the sending off.“It’s a difficult scoreline and it’s not easy at home,” Lampard said. “The first half was pretty good, we created some chances, better chances and we had them under a lot of pressure. Then a mistake to make it 2-0 and the red card makes it very difficult.“It feels very difficult to take the result, but a lot of circumstances that you can reflect on and say: ‘If, and if, and if.’ We need to be honest about that – we need to take chances in this league. It’s not a nice feeling.”The scoreline certainly lent weight to Fabian Hürzeler’s insistence that Brighton have no attacking concerns despite Danny Welbeck’s summer departure. Brighton have scored more goals and created more big chances than any other club in the Premier League this season – indeed, they have never started a top‑flight campaign with more goals.“It’s not about having one good goalscorer,” Hürzeler said. “It’s about the flexibility of having many goalscorers and a lot of players who have this desire to score. We were very efficient today and quite ruthless at the right moments in front of goal.”That was certainly true, beginning with a moment of mastery from ­Kostoulas to break the deadlock, when the Greek teenager showed great poise to control an aerial ball with his foot, nod it between two defenders and then fire into the bottom corner.That Brighton were not already behind by then was thanks to ­Verbruggen, who produced two excellent saves to deny Jack Rudoni, when palming a volley and a header to safety.Lampard publicly urged his ­players to “have belief” during the half‑time interval, but then followed two ­minutes that instantly extinguished Coventry’s hopes.View image in fullscreenFrank Lampard endures another glum day in the Premier League with Coventry.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAFirst came Brighton’s second goal, when Yalcouyé was played in behind the Coventry defence, and the Ivorian’s pace kept all at bay before calmly slotting past Carl Rushworth.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMoments later, the hosts were reduced to 10 men. At first glance, contact appeared accidental between Awoniyi and De Cuyper. But, to the refe­ree Tony Harrington’s credit, he spotted the Nigerian had led with his elbow, prompting a straight red card. To compound matters, the stadium announcer chose that period to tell fans that train cancellations meant there would be no departures from the stadium for 90 minutes after the final whistle.Thomas’s challenge to bring down Kostoulas inside his own box was as clear a penalty as will be awarded all season and Gross duly stuck the spotkick into the bottom corner.By the time Dunk sealed the rout with the finest strike of his career – smashed into the top corner from 35 yards – the mass exodus had already begun. It was an outrageous hit, with Dunk saying: “I shocked myself, but it was lovely.”That was followed in injury time by another excellent finish, this time from Ayari, curled from range into the ­bottom corner.The only other team to lose their first four Premier League games without scoring were Crystal Palace in 2017‑18. Palace finished 11th that season, but need to pull the emergency Roy Hodgson cord. ­Coventry will hope he is not required here.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueCoventry CityBrighton & Hove Albionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Kane helps Bayern edge Elversberg, Sassuolo stun Juventus | European club football | The Guardian
description: Harry Kane opened his Bundesliga account with the winner at Elversberg, while Sassuolo got the better of Juventus after a frantic finish
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Harry Kane opened his Bundesliga account with the winner at Elversberg, while Sassuolo got the better of Juventus after a frantic finish
Content: Harry Kane opens his Bundesliga account with the winning goal at promoted Elversberg.Photograph: Ronald Wittek/EPAView image in fullscreenHarry Kane opens his Bundesliga account with the winning goal at promoted Elversberg.Photograph: Ronald Wittek/EPAEuropean club footballEuropean football: Kane helps Bayern edge Elversberg, Sassuolo stun JuventusElversberg 1-2 Bayern; Sassuolo 3-2 JuventusBarcelona see off Levante, PSG end winless runAgenciesSun 13 Sep 2026 18.47 EDTFirst published on Sun 13 Sep 2026 13.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry Kane scored his firstBundesligagoal of the season to helpBayernMunichedge to a 2-1 win at promotedElversbergon Sunday. Handed the captain’s armband with skipper Manuel Neuer rested, Kane scored with 18 minutes remaining to break a 1-1 deadlock and put the defending champions on track for victory.Bayern had taken the lead through teenage Germany winger Lennart Karl, but Elversberg – who had won their opening two matches in their maiden top-flight campaign – levelled things up just after the hour mark thanks to a stunning curling effort from Maurice Krattenmacher.Kane scored 36 league goals last campaign, but after drawing a blank in his first two matches he told Dazn: “That’s football – sometimes you have to wait more than you’d have expected. It was nice to get the goal and the three points. It’s a tough place so we’re happy with the win. We probably haven’t reached our top level yet, but it’s still early days.”RB Leipzigbounced back from their midweek Champions League defeat at Como by thumping strugglersHamburg5-0 at home. The Norway winger Antonio Nusa was the best of the bunch for the hosts, scoring one goal and setting up two more, including one for Christopher Nkunku, his first since returning to Leipzig in August.Tidiam Gomis, Willi Orban and Rômulo also got on the scoresheet for Leipzig, who climbed to fifth in the table with the victory. Hamburg’s third heavy defeat in a row leaves the six-times German champions bottom of the table with a -12 goal difference.In ItalyJuventussuffered a 3-2 defeat after a frantic finish atSassuoloon Sunday. Sassuolo broke the deadlock in the 65th minute when Nemanja Matic slipped a precise ⁠pass into the area for Sebastiano Esposito, who finished coolly.Juventus levelled in the 82nd ​minute after Sassuolo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric misjudged a cross, ‌allowing Edon Zhegrova to tap ‌into an empty net. The hosts retook the lead through Scottish striker Kieron Bowie, who curled a first-time effort into the corner in the 89th minute.Zhegrova appeared to have rescued a point for Juventus when he fired home from the edge of the area in stoppage time, but Sassuolo had the final say. Four minutes into injury time, Vasilije Adzic curled a superb finish into the far corner to seal victory for Alberto Aquilani’s side with virtually the ‌last kick of the game.View image in fullscreenSassuolo celebrate after Vasilije Adzic’s dramatic stoppage-time winner against Juventus.Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/ReutersNapoliended a three-match losing run with a ⁠1-0 home win over ⁠Bologna. Midfielder Stanislav Lobotka turned in a second-half winner after Arthur Theate’s early header for the visitors was ruled offside by VAR. Elsewhere, Lassana Coulibaly scored twice asLecceearned a 3-2 home win overMonza.Inter host Udinese, Como entertain Parma and Roma travel to Torino on Monday evening.In Spain,Barcelonacontinued their perfect start to the ⁠season with a hard-fought 4-2 La Liga victory overLevantein Valencia ⁠on Sunday. Barça struck twice within the first 19 minutes, their goals coming from Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal.Just 42 ‌seconds into the second half, Barcelona were awarded ‌a penalty, won and converted by Lamine Yamal. An errant pass from Espart allowed Levante forward Iván Romero ‌to round goalkeeper Joan García and pass the ball into the net ​with 12 minutes to go.With two minutes remaining, Roger Brugue burst through multiple Barcelona challenges to score a second for Levante, but the hosts’ hopes of an unlikely comeback were definitively ​ended ​by a mazy run ​and finish from Karim Adeyemi ​in the ‌93rd minute.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenLamine Yamal (right) celebrates with Raphinha after scoring his first goal against Levante.Photograph: Biel Aliño/EPAAtlético Madridscored three late goals ​to beatReal Sociedad3-0, as new ​signings Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David scored their ​first goals since joining the club.The visitors took charge of a dull encounter when Grimaldo netted an 84th-minute penalty, ​before David doubled their lead ‌on ​the break six minutes later. Giuliano ​Simeone added a third in the 95th minute to complete the scoring for Atlético, who were without Julián Alvarez and Pablo Barrios due to muscle injuries.Adrian Nino’s late goal rescued a 1-1 draw forMálagaagainstCelta Vigo, who had dominated the game at Balaidos. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored his fifth goal in as many games asDeportivo A Coruñafought back to draw 1-1 withGetafe.Ferran Torres kept up his scoring form asParis Saint-Germainwon their first Ligue 1 match of the season at the fourth attempt, edging to a 1-0 victory against Brest.Torres took five minutes to put the visitors ahead, picking up ⁠a loose ball in midfield and passing to João Neves. The ball was worked to Ousmane Dembélé, whose back heel into Torres’ path gave him time and space to bend a low shot into the corner.Torres has now netted ⁠six goals in five outings since moving to the European champions, who move up to seventh after starting their league campaign with two draws and a defeat.Lillemoved top of the table on goal difference with a 2-0 triumph over Troyes, with Ethan Mbappé adding a late second after Tiago Santos’s opener.Lensfought back from two goals down ‌to draw 2-2 at another promoted side,Le Mans.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballBundesligaBayern MunichLa LigaBarcelonaRB LeipzigJuventusnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lauren James revels in free role as Chelsea show ‘respect’ by scoring five past Manchester United | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea dominated in a 5-0 away victory against Eva Olid’s Manchester United
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea dominated in a 5-0 away victory against Eva Olid’s Manchester United
Content: Lauren James and Keira Walsh (right) were both on the scoresheet for Chelsea.Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLauren James and Keira Walsh (right) were both on the scoresheet for Chelsea.Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueLauren James revels in free role as Chelsea show ‘respect’ by scoring five past Manchester UnitedSuzanne Wrackat Leigh Sports VillageSun 13 Sep 2026 09.41 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA swaggering Chelsea cast off any suggestion that they had lost the ability to kill off games, putting five goals past a worryingly lacklustre and lackadaisical Manchester United.Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea manager, said: “When you have the opportunity to really hurt a team, the best way to respect them is to score as many goals as you can, to create as many opportunities as you can.London City’s superstars brought down to earth in WSL defeat at West HamRead more“Of course, it’s never easy to see the other team or the other manager concede five goals because if I was the other team, I would be really sad. For me, showing respect to the opponent is having that desire and mentality to score as many goals as possible. That’s the difference between the great teams and the good teams.”United’s players and fans may have preferred disrespect if that is the case. Instead, it was another bruising result for the new manager, Eva Olid, and her side after an underwhelming performance in their2-1 defeatagainst London City Lionesses in the opening game of the season.Olid needed a result to give her some breathing room and her team some confidence, having had just three weeks to get used to one another before the start of the season, and this early into a project there has to be some grace.For their opponents this game had been talked about as something of a must‑win after the Blues wereheld to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villaon the opening weekend despite dominating that match.View image in fullscreenKeira Walsh scores Chelsea’s side's second goal from the edge of the box.Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesTo some extent the concern over Chelsea’s profligacy did not need to be too deep. They were at their creative best against Villa and were without the injured centre-forwards Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramírez while Aggie Beever-Jones, who led the line against the Midlands side, had not scored in the Women’s Super League since September 2025. The off-target Beever-Jones was relegated to the bench for the trip to United. Instead, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nüsken worked away interchangeably up front.The visitors were similarly fluid in other areas too, and that flexibility was super effective. Chelsea were unpredictable and James’s free‑to‑roam role put their star talent at the centre of everything.Lucy Bronze’s marauding forward yielded the opener when she sent a looping ball over the top and Dominique Janssen should have been first to it, but the United defender misread the fall of the ball and a stalking Wieke Kaptein nipped it away from her. The Dutch midfielder squared to Nüsken who fired in from close range.The second goal, which eluded them against Villa, arrived just over 10 minutes later. A diving header from the new recruit Andrea Medina cleared a cross whipped in from the left but the hard-working Bronze was there to meet it, clipping it into the path of Keira Walsh, who took a step and powered in from the edge of the box.The hosts’ heads dropped, which left their manager unhappy. “In football we know anything can happen,” Olid said. “You can be losing 2-0 and can end up winning. I don’t like the heads down. Heads up and we have to continue. Everything is about confidence.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionA very brief brighter spell for United after the break was snuffed out by the visiting team and James finally got on the scoresheet after the hour, latching on to Walsh’s defence‑splitting pass and shrugging off Janssen before sending a low drive into the net.Chelsea’s fourth goal rubbed salt in for a very wounded United side. Janssen, under no pressure, failed to respond to an ambitious burst from Kaptein and the Chelsea midfielder pickpocketed the centre-back and slipped the ball wide to the onrushing Ellie Carpenter, whose first effort was kept out by Phallon Tullis‑Joyce but her follow-up found the net.Bronze then added to United’s misery during the final minute of added time, hammering the ball in after Walsh knocked a corner back into the melee in the six-yard box.It became a training exercise for Chelsea and the hosts failed in their attempts to limit the damage. Things look as if they will get worse for Olid’s side before they get better, with a trip to the Emirates Stadium to play Arsenal coming up next weekend, but Olid said she will not divert from the style of football she wants the team to commit to playing.“If you start changing, then you are never going to build what you want to build,” she said. “It’s a process. I know it’s so hard, the process, because this beginning is hard. Nobody wants to lose games, but we have to be faithful to what we want to do, because I think that long term will give us the wins.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueManchester United WomenChelsea WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: WSL roundup: Arsenal rue misses in Palace draw, Manchester City crush Villa | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal had 30 attempts on goal but could not find a way past promoted Palace, while Manchester City showed no such profligacy against Aston Villa
Author: Emillia Hawkins
Headline: Arsenal had 30 attempts on goal but could not find a way past promoted Palace, while Manchester City showed no such profligacy against Aston Villa
Content: Crystal Palace celebrate a hard-earned point at the Emirates Stadium.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenCrystal Palace celebrate a hard-earned point at the Emirates Stadium.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersWomen's Super LeagueWSL roundup: Arsenal rue misses in Palace draw, Manchester City crush VillaGunners held at Emirates despite 30 attempts on goalCity win 4-1 at Aston Villa to extend perfect startEmillia HawkinsSun 13 Sep 2026 15.58 EDTFirst published on Sun 13 Sep 2026 14.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArsenal were left to rue 30 missed chances after dropping points in a 0-0 draw against Crystal Palace at the Emirates Stadium.The Gunners hit the target nine times and had almost 80% possession but could not convert their superiority into goals. Promoted Palace put on a resilient performance, with the goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin batting away attempts from Alessia Russo, Chloe Kelly and Mariona Caldentey to earn another clean sheet.Lauren James revels in free role as Chelsea show ‘respect’ by scoring five past Manchester UnitedRead moreThe reigning champions,Manchester City,continued their winning start to the campaign with a dominant 4-1 victory againstAston Villa. Jade Rose broke the deadlock for City in the early stages, tapping home after Akane Okuma failed to claim a corner. Assisted by Khadija Shaw, Mary Fowler doubled the advantage with a low-driven strike into the bottom-right of the net.Amalie Vangsgaard gave Andrée Jeglertz and his players a fright after converting Chasity Grant’s pass in the 42nd minute, but Shaw returned to the scoresheet after half-time to restore the two-goal cushion. City wrapped up the victory in added time when Lauren Hemp’s strike was deflected in by Mathilde Harviken.View image in fullscreenKhadija Shaw scores Manchester City’s third goal in their 4-1 win at Villa Park.Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/ReutersBrightoncame from two goals down to snatch a last-minute equaliser atBirmingham City. The promoted hosts took an early lead through Oceane Hurtre, who capitalised on a lapse in concentration from Caitlin Hayes before running into the box and slotting past Chiamaka Nnadozie.Lily Crosthwaite made it two in the second half with a low driven shot across the goalkeeper, but Brighton gathered momentum when Olivia García came off the bench to close the gap in the 77th minute. As Birmingham attempted to hold on for the win, Kiko Seike raced into the box with just a few seconds remaining and made the most of a small gap between Sophie Baggaley and the near post to score.At Goodison Park,Charltonfell to a 1-0 defeat byEvertonfollowing an own goal and two red cards. After a goalless first half, things quickly went downhill for the promoted side when Ashleigh Neville saw red for a high boot which caught Ruby Mace. With 13 minutes of normal time to play, the visitors found themselves behind when Holly McNamara’s cross deflected off the leg of Leighanne Robe and into the net. In the latter stages, Charlton went down to nine players after the substitute Hawa Cissoko received two yellow cards in quick succession.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLiverpoolcame from behind to earn a 1-1 draw againstTottenhamthanks to a 60th-minute header from Aurelie Csillag. Spurs took the lead just before half-time when Signe Gaupset’s effort was deflected in off the foot of Liverpool’s Sam Kerr. The hosts levelled things up at the hour-mark after Csillag got in front of Lize Kop to head home Fuka Nagano’s cross.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballArsenal WomenCrystal Palace WomenBrighton & Hove Albion WomenEverton WomennewsShareReuse this content

title: Rangers lay down Old Firm marker to send Celtic packing from Scottish League Cup | Scottish League Cup | The Guardian
description: Derek McInnes earned his first Old Firm win at Rangers with a resounding 3-0 victory against Celtic in the Scottish League Cup quarter-finals
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: Derek McInnes earned his first Old Firm win at Rangers with a resounding 3-0 victory against Celtic in the Scottish League Cup quarter-finals
Content: The Rangers captain, Dan Neil, wheels away after opening the scoring at Ibrox.Photograph: Craig Brough/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe Rangers captain, Dan Neil, wheels away after opening the scoring at Ibrox.Photograph: Craig Brough/ReutersScottish League CupRangers lay down Old Firm marker to send Celtic packing from Scottish League CupPaul MacInnesat Ibrox ParkSun 13 Sep 2026 09.38 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDerek McInnes has endured a much‑scrutinised start to life at Ibrox but theRangersmanager got the old ground bouncing here as his side dominated Celtic in front of an all-blue crowd to decide the first Old Firm encounter of the season.Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease. It also showcased a nascent identity for McInnes’s side, one defined by unbending physical commitment and lots and lots of sprinting. The quality of the football may have been patchy, but the commitment was enough to get the 51,212 home fans at the top of their voices.Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chantsRead moreWith away fans banned from Old Firm fixtures this season afterthe pitch invasionthat followed a Scottish Cup tie in March, the atmosphere was always likely to be partisan, if perhaps less heated than is customary. Before the match there was a brisk trade on both Graeme Souness flags and boiled sweets. Inside the ground the Union Bears ultras unveiled a tifo showcasing the apparently resonant moment when Rangers’ Ian Ferguson grabbed Celtic’s Mike Galloway by the lapels during a clash in 1993. A deep cut of a banner, it did a good job of setting the tone for what was to follow.McInnes said: “I’m delighted. The performance we gave today was the one required to overcome a team likeCeltic. I thought the game demanded the players’ full attention and I’m delighted they’ve managed to deliver that. We’ve seen the strength of the club today and it does the players no harm to understand what this match means to so many people.”Rangers went about the match with an intensity that Celtic struggled to equal from the off, some of their players looking distinctly overawed by the occasion. The former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was among them, flapping at two early openings, but he could do nothing about the opening goal when it arrived in the 22nd minute. After a Celtic counter broke down Rangers immediately turned play around with a long ball to the Celtic area where Cameron Carter‑Vickers failed to properly clear. Kelsy picked up the loose ball, slipped it to Neil and the captain, signed on a free transfer from Sunderland in the summer, placed an excellent shot just inside Johnstone’s left‑hand post.After seizing the advantage, Rangers went on to dominate the second half and a second goal appeared inevitable. It duly arrived when a free-kick from the impressive James Penrice was flicked on by Ryan Naderi to the back post where Kelsy clipped his effort around the keeper and inside the left-hand post.View image in fullscreenKevin Kelsy lashes in Rangers’ second goal around the hour.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PANeil then took matters into his own hands with a quarter of an hour remaining as he controlled a loose ball on the edge of the Celtic area and wrapped a shot into the top corner to unleash delirium in the Copland Stand. “I haven’t scored many goals in my career, so to come away with a brace is immense,” Neil said.It was perhaps just as well for O’Neill that his supporters had been denied access to this match. Celtic began with a calmness that suggested confidence. Ultimately it was more likely to have reflected timidity. The Bhoys were unable to get a foot on the ball at all in the second half, and the big-money signing Kasper Høgh looked lost at the tip of the Celtic attack before he was substituted on 65 minutes.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We were well beaten in the end, on the day we were second best,” O’Neill said. “There has to be a realisation how big this game is, it’s still one of the great fixtures in European football if not the world. We’ve got to know that. We have to learn from it. Hopefully it’s a wake‑up call.”Rangers will play Aberdeen in the semi-finals, but McInnes was still being asked about Rangers’stuttering start to the seasonafter this match, generating the timeless response: “Why are you pissing on my chips?”After this result the Rangers manager can at least look forward with optimism and he could be set to unleash the spirit of Ian Ferguson again as early as next weekend when a second Old Firm derby awaits, this time at Celtic Park.Explore more on these topicsScottish League CupRangersCelticmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Spygate saga continues to haunt Southampton as case drags on | Southampton | The Guardian
description: Tonda Eckert’s future remains uncertain after FA punishment yet to be decided
Author: Sam Cunningham
Headline: Tonda Eckert’s future remains uncertain after FA punishment yet to be decided
Content: Tonda Eckert is still awaiting his fate after last season’s spying scandal.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTonda Eckert is still awaiting his fate after last season’s spying scandal.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesSouthamptonSpygate saga continues to haunt Southampton as case drags onManager Tonda Eckert’s future remains in the balance with the FA yet to decide over a suitable punishmentSam Cunninghamat St Mary's StadiumSun 13 Sep 2026 03.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFifty seconds was all it took for the chant to begin. “You know what you are, you know what you are, cheating bastards, you know what you are,” bellowed theBristol Cityfans, starting up a cry heard from every away contingent coming to St Mary’s Stadium this season. The Southampton supporters responded with sarcastic applause, then drowned out the noise with songs of their own.This is what life is now like for Southampton afterMay’s spying scandal– a saga whose full consequences are still unknown and could have ramifications for the season ahead. The English Football League acted swiftly afterphotographs emerged of a junior staff member hiding behind a treeto film a Middlesbrough training session, expelling Southampton from the Championship play-offs and deducting four points after the club admitted multiple spying offences, including on Oxford United and Ipswich. The Football Association’s case against Tonda Eckert, the manager, is taking far longer. And patience is wearing thin.Championship roundup: Middlesbrough win seven-goal thriller; Burnley lose againRead moreThe incident left a deep stain on Southampton’s reputation, one that will take time to fade and will leave an indelible mark on their history. Fans initially felt a mixture of fury and embarrassment – their promotion hopes snatched away over smartphone footage of a rival’s training session. Still, it has not stopped them flocking to St Mary’s this season: attendances were a shade under 30,000 for visits from Stoke, Millwall and Swansea and a season-high of 30,132 made Saturday’s Bristol City match almost a sell-out.“Initially I was disappointed and angry,” says Alex Watson, a 31-year-old Saints fan, outside the stadium before kick-off. “Then you go through all the stages up to acceptance.”Frustration is now turning towards the FA for taking so long to confirm what punishment – if any – Eckert will face after being charged individually by the governing body. A fine or short ban would be manageable. But Bev Priestman wasbanned for a year by Fifa, while manager of Canada, after two staff members used a drone to spy on an opponent at the Paris Olympics, so there is precedent for a lengthy suspension. That would likely see Eckert be removed as manager.It is nearly two months since theFA charged Eckert with misconduct, even though the EFL’s independent panel took a matter of days to determine Eckert authorised the spying and that it was a“contrived and determined plan from the top down”.“The mood generally is the FA needs to make a decision,” Watson says. “They need to get on and do something about it, one way or the other.”There is a lingering sense of inconsistency between sanctions for big clubs and the rest – an irritation shared across the country. Chelsea receivedfines and suspended transfer bansfrom the Premier League and FA for systemic breaches of agent rules between 2009 and 2022. Yet Southampton have been kicked out of a competition, docked four points and may lose their manager for filming some training sessions.If anything, Southampton fans have begun leaning into the pantomime-villain role. On the hour, a chant of “We spy when we want, we spy when we want, we are Southampton, we spy when we want” broke out. Within a minute, Cyle Larin had put them two in front with his second of the match.View image in fullscreenCyle Larin scores to put Southampton 2-0 up against Bristol City.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesWhile awaiting a verdict, the club have been preparing for all eventualities. During a preseason friendly against Preussen Münster, Eckert watched from the stands while his assistant, Ben Garner, took charge in the dugout – practising how operations might work if the German is handed a touchline ban.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe scandal did not deter summer signings. The goalkeeper Daniel Peretz was a £6m coup from Bayern Munich, agreeing to make his loan permanent after playing through the storm. Larin made a similar commitment and the Canadian forward has scored eight goals in nine games. The fan favourite James Ward-Prowse, a star of their last Premier League spell, decided to return.Early indications are that the team can be promotion challengers. Late goals from Kuryu Matsuki and Finn Azaz completed a thumping win. After the final whistle, Eckert walked around the Northam and the Itchen Stands applauding; the fans stood to applaud back. Eckert, who returned after the summer uncertain how fans would react, says their backing “means everything” to him.Asked if he has found it easy to block out the looming FA decision, he said: “I wouldn’t call it easy. But life isn’t always easy, if you have big goals then you need to find a way.” He added: “The fans have every right to react differently to the situation, how it’s evolved over the last season. I would’ve respected every reaction and decision from the club, the board and the supporters. Either you can forgive or you can’t. That’s not my decision. It’s just to accept how the reaction is.”Had Southampton not started the season with a four-point deduction, they would be level on points with the top of the table. Losing the manager behind it would be another cruel twist.Explore more on these topicsSouthamptonChampionshipFootball LeagueThe FABristol CityfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: World’s top tennis players call truce in prize-money battle with grand slams | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Jannik Sinner and Aryna Sabalenka were the most vocal of the leading players but their 18-month campaign comes to an end after the US Open
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Jannik Sinner and Aryna Sabalenka were the most vocal of the leading players but their 18-month campaign comes to an end after the US Open
Content: Jannik Sinner after winning Wimbledon 2026, beating Alex Zverev in four sets. Sinner can concentrate on his tennis after the end of the prize-money campaign.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenJannik Sinner after winning Wimbledon 2026, beating Alex Zverev in four sets. Sinner can concentrate on his tennis after the end of the prize-money campaign.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianTennisWorld’s top tennis players call truce in prize-money battle with grand slams18-month campaign comes to an end after US OpenSinner and Sabalenka most vocal of leading playersMatt HughesSun 13 Sep 2026 19.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe world’s leading tennis players have agreed a truce in their long-running battle with the grand slam tournaments over prize money, welfare and player consultation.In a statement released after the men’s US Open final on Sunday the players announced they would stop their 18-month campaign of agitating against the grand slam tournaments, which culminated in a media boycott at the French Open this year, a planfirst revealed in May.Alexander Zverev claims first US Open after four-set battle with Ben SheltonRead moreA similar boycott planned for Wimbledon was called off after the All England LawnTennisClub made concessions.Jannik Sinner and the US Open finalist Aryna Sabalenka were the most vocal of the players lobbying on behalf of the locker room, with Carlos Alcaraz last month withdrawing from the campaign.The players have been calling for a greater share of the tournament revenues from the four major tournaments to be paid in prize money, a contribution from the grand slam events to player welfare and pension provision, and a formal role in decision-making through the creation of a player council.It was revealed in August all four tournaments had agreed tocreate a grand slam player advisory council, a move which appears to have been crucial in bringing players back into the fold.“Now that a formal council exists to carry this work forward, the public phase of the campaign led by the unified group of top players comes to a close,” their statement read.View image in fullscreenAryna Sabalenka was one of the more vocal players lobbying on behalf of the locker room.Photograph: Eduardo Muñoz/Reuters“Players reserve the right to restart the campaign should the Council fail to deliver on these aims. The players involved in the campaign will be making no further public comment as a unified group on these issues at this time.“The players will now work directly with the grand slams to establish the council, through which players themselves will be directly consulted and able to negotiate on an ongoing basis.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe players’ statement claimed they had achieved victories in all three areas of their campaign, as the US Tennis Association agreed to make a $2m (£1.48m) contribution to player welfare at the US Open this year, although their target of 22% of the grand slam tournament revenues to be allocated to prize money remains elusive.While prize money has increased significantly it remains at about 15% across all the slams and the French Open is the only grand slam tournament to indicate it will introduce a revenue-sharing formula.“Since the players’ formal proposal was submitted on 31 July 2025, prize money across these grand slam tournaments has grown to $415.6m in total, with players estimating that more than $30m of that reflects incremental gains above the rate of growth the years before the campaign began,” the players said.“This stands as a testament to the gains made possible by concerted, unified player action in an individual sport and by constructive dialogue with the grand slams and tournament organisers. The players look to the council to build on this progress and continue pursuing the aims not yet fully achieved.”Explore more on these topicsTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Josh Kerr bags $150,000 for 1500m victory at Ultimate Championship | Athletics | The Guardian
description: The Scot won with ease ahead of Yared Nuguse and Cameron Myers, while Charlotte Henrich’s final leg earned Britain silver in the 4x400m mixed relay
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: The Scot won with ease ahead of Yared Nuguse and Cameron Myers, while Charlotte Henrich’s final leg earned Britain silver in the 4x400m mixed relay
Content: Josh Kerr produced a substantial lead over the rest of the field to win the men’s 1500m.Photograph: Tibor Illyes/EPAView image in fullscreenJosh Kerr produced a substantial lead over the rest of the field to win the men’s 1500m.Photograph: Tibor Illyes/EPAAthleticsJosh Kerr bags $150,000 for 1500m victory at Ultimate ChampionshipScot wins with ease ahead of Nuguse and MyersHenrich’s final leg earns Britain silver in mixed relaySean Inglein BudapestSun 13 Sep 2026 16.21 EDTLast modified on Sun 13 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThroughout Josh Kerr’s perfect season, he has made the sublime look routine. So when the bell rang for the final lap of the men’s Ultimate 1500m final, with the Scot in third and closing on the leader, Yared Nuguse, the next 53 seconds felt preordained.So it proved. First Kerr sauntered past Robert Farken into second. Then with 250m remaining, he scootered past Nuguse. The 20‑year‑old Australian star Cam Myers chased valiantly but Kerr smoothly nursed a three-metre lead to the finish.‘Just making a joke’: Usain Bolt retracts claim stairs got him out of breathRead moreAs Kerr crossed the line in 3min 29.35sec, with Myers 0.33 back, he cupped his hand to his ear. The sound he was hearing? The adoration of the crowd, and the kerching of the $150,000 (£111,000) first prize. “To be honest, I didn’t feel amazing in the warmup,” Kerr said. “But these are the things you have to overcome.”Asked about Myers, who won the Diamond League final last week, Kerr replied: “He’s an awesome athlete but I was able to peek over the screen. I pressed again at 120m, and then the gap didn’t change, and I knew that at that point I had it.”The only shame was that Jakob Ingebrigtsen, who won a brilliant 5,000m victory on Friday, decided to skip what would have been a mouthwatering clash. But Kerr was generous to his great rival afterwards, describing Ingebrigtsen’s victory as “very impressive” and praising his decision to rest up to protect the longevity of his career.Kerr will now take a holiday having ended his season having shattered the world mile record and walked away with three major prizes: world indoor championship gold over 3,000m, Commonwealth Games gold over the mile, and now the Ultimate Championship trophy.
